lens: LP economics and microstructure: LVR per session tier, break-even fees, markouts, block-time effects on arbitrage loss. Every issue judged by what it does to a passive LP's expected P&L.

issues.reasoning: On an LP P&L basis 500/350/300 is not well set. The measured per-tier variance (tiervar_all.json: SPY overnight/open variance ratio 0.26, closed/open 0.025) and the reproduced break-even ladder (be3.py output: 8.2 / 1.9 / 2.3 bps over 7d, 4.5 / 1.1 over the post-routing 48h) put the open tier at or under break-even and the overnight and closed tiers far above theirs. The shipped 1.00/0.70/0.60 shape taxes the cheap hours and undercharges the toxic ones. V's 750/450/250 (ProposedFees.t.sol:31) gives 1.00/0.60/0.33, which is closer to the break-even shape than the current ladder and lifts the open tier above the 7d break-even without reaching the 35 bps rival. R's 'well set' rests on a competitive read (the 1 bp subsidised venues) that says nothing about whether LPs cover LVR. Caveats: V's own section 3.2 (line 331-333) claimed overnight was 92% as volatile as the session, which the addendum's 730-day data contradicts; the elasticity evidence for 'no share is lost' is cross-sectional and weak (V line 137-139 admits this). Also V's shipped script goes to 900, not 750; the 750 is only in the scratch test.
evidence: be3.py reproduced output: SPY OPEN 7d break-even 8.2 bps vs 5.00 charged (1.6x gap)
issues.would_change_my_mind: A per-window markout on SPY showing LPs are net positive at 5 bps open (i.e. realised arb loss well below sigma^2/8 * k because of fast blocks and the fee band), or evidence that UR-routed retail volume falls by more than the fee ratio when the open tier rises.

issues.reasoning: NVDA is the clearest LP-economics failure in the set. Break-even at the open is 22-27 bps against 7 charged (be3.py: 3.2x-3.9x gap; be_all.json OPEN_7d 2751 pips). Overnight break-even 3.9-7.2 bps against 4. R's 'well set, the lever is TVL' would add capital to a pool where every dollar of TVL loses to LVR faster than it earns fees. V's 1000/750/300 (test) or 1400/900/250 (script) moves toward break-even while staying under the 35 bps and 110 bps NVDA pools on the same chain. The opening spike and close ramp stay on in both. Note V's original document (line 313) said 'do not raise its level' and the addendum reversed that on the LVR measurement; the reversal is the correct call for LPs. The counter-argument is the 5 bps v3 venue holding 96-98% of the pair, but Fables has 0.1% share at 7 bps already, so there is no routed flow to lose.
evidence: be3.py output: NVDA OPEN 7d break-even 27.0 bps, 48h 22.4 bps vs 7.00 charged
issues.would_change_my_mind: A markout showing realised NVDA LP loss is a small fraction of the sigma^2/8 * k figure (fast blocks plus a fee band can cut it a lot), or evidence that NVDA volume is mostly non-toxic and would evaporate above 10 bps.

issues.reasoning: GLD at 500/350 is at or below its LVR break-even: be_all.json GLD OPEN_7d 998 pips, 48h 408; OVERNIGHT_7d 377, 48h 179. R's anchor (PAXG/USDC 5 bps on mainnet) is a venue this chain's flow cannot reach and it ignores k: with k=75.5 Fables GLD liquidity is 75x as exposed to LVR as a full-range pool. V's 1500/1000/300 clears break-even with margin and remains half the 3000 pips venue. Two caveats reduce confidence: V's 72% share table is one window (DATA-PACK line 139 shows Fables doing 2.2x that rival's volume on 08-27, so share is unstable); and the GLD overnight variance was built with an ES fill, not GC (see factual errors), so the level of the overnight break-even is less certain than V presents.
issues.would_change_my_mind: A GC-filled recomputation of GLD tier variance that lowers the overnight break-even well below 350 pips, or a markout showing GLD LPs are already positive at 4 bps realised.

issues.reasoning: Measured GLD variance is nearly flat across the weekday (overnight/open 0.83) and collapses on the weekend (closed/open 0.068). R's concept, flat weekday with a weekend-only discount, describes gold's hours more accurately than an equity-shaped ladder; V's 1500/1000 (1.00/0.67) discounts the overnight by a third when the variance says 17%. But R's weekend tier (3 bps vs 5, ratio 0.6) is far above the measured 0.07 ratio, while V's 300/1500 = 0.20 is closer; and R's 5 bps level sits at the 48h open break-even and below the 7d one. On the break-even-in-pips measure (which folds in volume per hour) overnight break-even is only 0.38x open because GLD's on-chain flow is heavier outside US hours, so both ladders cover it. Neither fixes the structural mismatch: the hook's CLOSED window runs Friday 16:00 ET to Monday 00:00 ET (SessionLib.classify lines 91-93), while gold reopens Sunday 18:00 ET; Sunday evening prices at the closed tier under both proposals, and the calendar has no knob for it (setSessionHours cannot move the weekend rule).
issues.would_change_my_mind: A GC-based tier variance showing the weekday overnight materially quieter than the open, which would favour V's 0.67 shape; or on-chain evidence that Sunday-evening GLD flow is toxic enough to justify a hook change.

issues.reasoning: The census diagnoses the structural change: UR went from 11 swaps across five pools pre-approval to 1,426 of 2,772 ETH swaps (51.4% by count). But by volume the UR is only 22.7% of ETH and 22.8% of SPY; the remaining three quarters comes from a handful of contract senders (0xb055, 0x8f10, 0x1521, 0x8611 carry $520k of $929k on ETH), which is consistent with arbitrage responding to retail flow rather than retail flow itself. So the surge is partly diagnosed (source of the new retail leg) and partly not (the persistence and toxicity of the larger contract leg). For fee decisions this matters less than R implies: the case for raising NVDA and GLD rests on 7d break-evens that are already well above current floors regardless of the surge, while the case that SPY 'clears LVR post-routing' (V addendum line 503) depends on surge volume and is the fragile one. Act on the tiers where the 7d break-even is unambiguous; treat the 48h post-routing numbers as optimistic. V's headline 51.4% should always be quoted as swap count, not volume.
issues.would_change_my_mind: A sender-level markout showing the large contract senders are not adverse (which would make the surge benign and the 48h break-evens trustworthy), or a collapse of UR share back toward zero.

issues.reasoning: R's claim that the calendar is UTC-hardcoded and drifts an hour in November is wrong on inspection. SessionLib.utcOffsetFromDate (lines 175-184) implements the second-Sunday-of-March / first-Sunday-of-November rule and returns EDT or EST accordingly; MarketCalendar exposes dstMode with FIXED_EST/FIXED_EDT escape hatches (lines 44, 136-140). The switch is day-granular (midnight ET rather than 02:00) but both switch days are Sundays, when every tier is CLOSED, so fee output is unaffected. I verified the arithmetic: for Mar 1 on a Sunday the rule yields the 8th, on a Monday the 14th. V does not address DST, so neither document is correct on the issue as posed; the code is.
issues.would_change_my_mind: A deployed hook bytecode that differs from this source, or a configured dstMode of FIXED_EDT on the live contracts.

issues.reasoning: Fee parity with the 90%-share winner does not make AAPL well set for its LPs: be_all.json puts AAPL's open break-even at 12.5-22.6 bps and overnight at 7.6-10.1 bps against 5/3.5 charged, on k=37. V's 800/500/250 is directionally right but still under break-even. The whole pool is $2.3k TVL and $2.8k/day, with k measured on 33 swaps, so every number here is noisy and the decision is nearly academic. What is not academic: R's framing ('the gap is depth') would seed capital into a pool priced below LVR. If AAPL is ever reseeded it should go in at V's ladder or higher.
issues.would_change_my_mind: A larger-sample k and volume measurement on AAPL showing break-even under 5 bps.

issues.reasoning: Both raise, and on break-even both land in range: META OPEN_7d 572 / 48h 238 pips, OVERNIGHT 710 / 362. V's 900/600/250 tracks the measured variance shape better (META overnight/open 0.44, closed/open 0.03; V's ladder 1.00/0.67/0.28 versus R's 1.00/0.70/0.50). R's 500 pips closed tier taxes a window with near-zero LVR for no LP benefit. But R's specification carries what V's lacks: a fixed duration, a rollback trigger (share drop over 20%) and an explicit success metric. Note the be_all overnight break-even is above the open on META because overnight volume per hour is lower, so the overnight tier deserves at least V's 600. Best specification is V's numbers under R's test protocol, with the success metric switched to LP markout rather than share.
evidence: FEE-AND-APR-REVIEW.md (no META-specific section; ladder only in the test file)
issues.would_change_my_mind: Evidence that META's weekend flow is toxic (which would justify R's 500 closed tier), or a markout showing 10 bps open already loses routed retail.

issues.reasoning: 'Recalibrate down' is not justified now on the LP numbers, and R itself ranks markouts first (line 115: 'markout study per fee-window; then recalibrate C down'). The V-side claim that the keeper clears sigma^2/8 is contradicted by the data pack and by res.json: fee APR / k is 2.68% (24h), 2.11% (48h), 0.73% (7d) against sigma^2/8 of 3.1-3.8% at the 50-55% realised sigma the keeper series records (lvr7d.json mean s 49.9). Cutting C by 30% would push a pool that already fails the naive LVR test further into deficit. The fast-block argument (arXiv 2404.05803) is real and is the reason the naive test may overstate realised loss, but it argues for measuring, not for cutting on a mainnet-derived haircut. The keeper series also shows the fee pinned at the 3000 cap repeatedly (lvr7d.json), so the top of the curve is where a markout would be most informative.
evidence: /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/res.json F-ETH a24 118.9, a48 93.6, a7 32.5; k 44.3 from DATA-PACK line 13
issues.would_change_my_mind: Per-window markouts showing poked-high windows have LP loss well below the fee collected (which would justify trimming the top of the curve), or a measured block-time-adjusted LVR for this chain that falls below the realised 8.9 bps.

issues.reasoning: Not orthogonal; sequencing matters. LVR scales with k * TVL * sigma^2/8, fees scale with volume. Seeding TVL into NVDA at 7 bps, where break-even is 22-27 bps, increases the dollar loss to arbitrageurs roughly in proportion to the capital added unless volume rises 3-4x with it, which depth alone does not guarantee (UR routing is not fee-blind, see I11). The same holds for the SPY/NVDA cross: be_all.json OPEN_7d 561-774 pips against 500 charged. Seeding is a sound growth lever only after the floors are above break-even. On the other side, more depth does attract routed retail (the least toxic flow), which lowers the fee needed; so the two work together once ordered fee first, TVL second. R's framing 'rather than change fees' is the part that is wrong for LPs.
issues.would_change_my_mind: Evidence that NVDA volume scales super-linearly with depth (so that seeded TVL lowers the break-even below 7 bps), or a markout showing NVDA LPs are positive at current fees.

issues.reasoning: Half of the law is supported and half is over-stated, and its implication runs against R's own 'well set' verdicts. Supported: AAPL at fee parity with 30x depth and 90% share is a clean depth-wins case (R line 36), and the census shows the deepest SPY rival (0xfe2a, $720k TVL, 34.99 bps) receiving 3,673 of the UR's SPY swaps against 671 for the 6.25 bps pool and 287 for Fables, i.e. routed flow follows depth even at a 5.6x fee premium. Over-stated: 'comparable-fee' is not a condition the data needs, and 'ultra-low fee wins arb flow regardless of depth' is asserted from a mainnet example not checked here. Implication: if routed flow follows depth rather than fee within the 5-35 bps range, a Fables raise from 5 to 7.5-10 bps does not lose routed flow, which is V's conclusion. The residual risk is on the smallest tickets (median $105 per V line 59), where price impact is negligible and the fee is the whole cost, so a best-execution router should be fee-sensitive; the 0xfe2a evidence says in practice it is not, for reasons nobody has diagnosed.
evidence: /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/ur_now.json (rival SPY 0xfe2a urC 3673 of 4951; 0xe592 671 of 5350; Fables SPY 287 of 1659)
issues.would_change_my_mind: A routing-log study showing the UR chooses 0xfe2a for reasons unrelated to depth (a hard-coded default, a quoter exclusion), or a post-raise observation that Fables' UR share drops faster than volume elasticity would predict.

lens: Competitive positioning and flow: who routes where and why, what incumbents charge, whether routed retail or arbitrage flow is at stake when a fee moves, and what share and volume evidence actually shows.

issues.reasoning: On the flow question, V is right that no routed share is at stake in a raise. The decisive datum is the rival 34.99 bps SPY pool: 74.8% of its volume arrives via the UniversalRouter and it did $1.28M on 08-27, more than double Fables; routed flow is going to the MOST expensive pool on the pair, so a move from 5 to 7.5 bps cannot be what loses it. Fables' own SPY routed share is 22.8% of dollars; the next two senders (0x39b3 20.6%, 0x0000 12.9%) are arb, which a raise sheds by design. R's 'well set' also fails the LVR check: the 7d open-tier break-even is 8.2 bps against 5.0 charged. However V's overnight tier is not supported by V's own measurement: be3.py gives SPY overnight break-even 1.1-1.9 bps, so 350 already clears and 450 is a raise on top of an argument (the 92% overnight vol claim in V 3.2) that V's own 730-day data withdrew (overnight variance is 0.26x open). Measured shape argues for roughly 750/250/250, not 750/450/250.
evidence: ur_now.json: rival SPY 0xfe2a swaps 4951, UR 3673 (74.2%), UR vol $603k of $806k (74.8%); Fables SPY UR 22.8% of $, 0x39b38686a1 20.6%, 0x0000 12.9%
be3.py output: F-SPY OPEN 7d break-even 8.2 bps vs 5.00 (1.6x); OVERNIGHT 7d 1.9 / 48h 1.1 vs 3.50
tiervar_all.json: SPY OVERNIGHT/OPEN variance ratio 0.26 (sigma 19.5/10.0/3.1%) vs V line 324 claiming 92%
issues.would_change_my_mind: A per-window markout or a two-week A/B showing Fables' UR swap count or UR dollar share fell after the raise while the 625 and 3499 pools' held; or evidence the 3499 pool's UR flow is a routing artefact (e.g. the only pool on some path) rather than a real preference.

issues.reasoning: Fables holds 0.1-0.3% of NVDA at 7 bps against a v3 pool at 5 bps holding 96-99%; UR share is only 10.1% of swaps / 6.3% of dollars, and the top senders are arb (0x6ddb 31.7%, 0xb055 12.0%). There is no routed share to lose, so the only flow a raise to 10 bps costs is arb flow, which is the flow losing LPs money: break-even at the open is 22-27 bps against 7. R's 'lever is TVL' is true but seeding capital into a pool 3-4x under its LVR break-even hands the seed to arbitrageurs. So V's open raise is right and R's 'well set' is wrong on LP economics. V's overnight 750 (0.75x open) is not supported: measured overnight break-even is 3.3-6.2 bps and the variance shape is 0.15-0.23x open; 400 was already near the mark. V's body (line 313 'Do not raise its level') and addendum (1400) contradict each other, which weakens the specification but not the direction.
evidence: now.json: R-NVDA-v3-500 v24 $59.8M, TVL $3.1M; F-NVDA v24 $178k, TVL $42.7k
be3.py: F-NVDA OPEN 7d 27.0 / 48h 22.4 bps vs 7.00; OVERNIGHT 7d 6.2 / 48h 3.3 vs 4.00
issues.would_change_my_mind: Evidence that the v3 pool's routed flow is fee-marginal at 7 vs 10 bps (it is not at 5 vs 7 today), or a markout showing the arb flow at 7 bps is already unprofitable for the arb and therefore not costing LPs.

issues.reasoning: R's anchor (PAXG/USDC on mainnet at 5 bps) is the wrong market: nobody on Robinhood Chain routes against mainnet. On this chain the GLD/USDG venues charge 3000 and 10000 pips, and the 3000 pool did $984k over 7d on $150k TVL, so demand exists at 30 bps. Fables' GLD routed share is 22.6% of dollars and would not leave at 15 bps against a 30 bps rival; the largest sender (0x6505, 34.9% of dollars, 1084 swaps, also 26.8% of the rival SPY pool) is arb and is the flow a raise sheds. The 7d open-tier break-even is ~10 bps against 5 charged. So V's direction and its staging (1500 then re-measure share) are right. But V's headline is stale and overstated: '72% share / 7.6x too cheap' comes from a window when the 3000 pool did $592k; on 08-27 it did $54k against Fables' $135k, so Fables is now the largest GLD venue by 24h volume. A 3x raise will cut that headline volume (it is mostly arb), which DATA-PACK's marketing leans on. Decide knowing that.
evidence: ur_now.json: F-GLD 0x65050a9b7e 34.9% of $ (1084 swaps), UR 22.6% of $; same sender is 26.8% of rival SPY 0xe592
DATA-PACK.md lines 129, 139, 275-277 (2.2x incumbent volume on a day the incumbent collapsed 292k -> 66k)
issues.would_change_my_mind: The 3000-pip pool's volume proving to be self-LP wash (R's caveat 2), which would mean there is no real 30 bps demand; or Fables' UR GLD swap count falling after Stage 1.

issues.reasoning: Both agree the weekend is a discount window (GC is shut Fri 17:00 to Sun 18:00 ET). The disagreement is overnight, and the measurement sides with R: GLD overnight variance is 0.83x the open (sigma 19.2 vs 17.5%), the flattest of any asset measured, because gold price discovery runs ~23h. An equity-style overnight discount (V's 1000 vs 1500, 0.67x) discounts the hours the arb channel is live, which R correctly identifies. The hook can express R's shape: setPoolConfig imposes no ordering on the three floors, so overnightFloor == openFloor validates. Two qualifications. First, V's closed tier (0.2x open) is much closer to the measured 0.07x than R's 0.6x. Second, the CLOSED variance in allvar.py is constructed as zero except for Sunday evening, which is an assumption; tokenised gold proxies trade on-chain all weekend, so gold's weekend LVR is likely understated for both documents. Neither calendar fits gold's real 17:00-18:00 ET daily break or its 13:30 COMEX settle; the equity bells do not map.

issues.would_change_my_mind: A per-tier markout on GLD showing overnight LP losses per dollar traded are materially below open-session losses; or weekend on-chain gold variance measured from a 24/7 proxy (PAXG/XAUt) showing the closed tier should not be discounted at all.

issues.reasoning: For a fee decision the question is not where every dollar came from but whether the flow at risk is fee-elastic. The census answers that: routed (UR) flow is ~23% of dollars on ETH, SPY and GLD and, per the 34.99 bps SPY pool, is not choosing pools by fee; the identified non-UR senders are arb contracts that a raise is meant to shed. That is enough to act on direction. It is not enough to size a raise, and R has a point neither document addresses: the surge (ETH $53k on 08-23 to $953k on 08-26) starts on the routing-approval day, but that is also the points-programme start (24 Aug 02:00 UTC), and points accrue on fees earned by LPs, which invites wash. The UR count share (51.4%) overstates the routed dollar share (22.7%). R's 'gates everything' is too strict; V's census diagnoses one component and treats it as the whole.

DATA-PACK.md lines 42-45 (approval Monday 08-24 ~05:00 UTC) and line 145 (points programme 24 Aug 02:00 UTC)
issues.would_change_my_mind: A sender-level breakdown showing the 77% non-UR growth is dominated by a few addresses that are also LPs in the same pools (wash for points), which would mean the surge is not fee-elastic in the way assumed and could vanish with the programme.

issues.reasoning: R's claim is wrong on inspection. SessionLib.utcOffsetFromDate implements the US statutory rule (second Sunday of March, first Sunday of November) and MarketCalendar exposes a dstMode (AUTO / FIXED_EST / FIXED_EDT) override. The switch is day-granular, but both switch days are Sundays when every session reads CLOSED, so fee output is unaffected. A test anchors a winter and a summer instant to the expected ET second-of-day. The offset is derived from the UTC civil date rather than the ET date, which only matters in the ET evening of the switch Saturday and is again inside CLOSED. There is no November drift. V's side (DATA-PACK line 50) states this correctly. The only real calendar gap for gold is holidays: the baked table is NYSE, and COMEX trades on several NYSE holidays.

CalendarLib.sol lines 95-105 (_ctx applies offset from UTC civil date)
issues.would_change_my_mind: A deployed hook instance found with dstMode pinned to FIXED_EDT, or a live read of sessionAt on a November weekday showing OPEN at 13:30 UTC.

issues.reasoning: On flow, R's diagnosis holds: at exact in-session parity (5 bps) with the v3 pool, Fables gets ~3% of the pair on 1/30th the depth, so the missing share is depth, not price. Raising AAPL will neither gain nor lose routed flow because there is none to speak of ($2.9k/day on $2.6k TVL). V's 800/500/250 is therefore harmless but also pointless until the pool is seeded. The one thing R gets wrong is calling 5 bps 'well set' as an LP price: AAPL's open-session variance is 2.8x SPY's (sigma 32.5% vs 19.5%) and the measured break-even is 12-22 bps, so if the pool is ever reseeded its ladder should be priced to variance, not copied from SPY. The fee is exonerated for the share gap, not validated as a price.
issues.would_change_my_mind: A seeding plan for AAPL, at which point the LVR break-even becomes the binding argument and V's ladder (or steeper) is the right starting point.

issues.reasoning: Both raise META to about the same open level (1000 vs 900 pips) and both cite rivals at 30-35 bps. R is better specified as a competitive experiment: a fixed duration, a share-based revert trigger (>20% share loss), and an explicit acknowledgment that rival volume may be wash so the test is designed to be safe either way. V gives numbers without a test protocol; META is not discussed anywhere in the V document body, only in ProposedFees.t.sol. V's shape is better, though: R's 500 closed is 0.5x open against a measured closed variance of 0.03x open, so R taxes the dead weekend; V's 250 is closer. Best specification is R's protocol with V's closed tier. Note UR is only 1.5% of META swaps, so there is essentially no routed flow to protect and the >20% share trigger will mostly be measuring arb departure.
evidence: ur_now.json: F-META 736 swaps, UR 11 (1.5%), UR $ 1.3%; top senders 0xa633 24.0%, 0x37b3 19.9%
issues.would_change_my_mind: Identification of META's rival pools and their UR shares; if they take real routed flow at 30 bps the share trigger should be defined against that flow specifically rather than total volume.

issues.reasoning: R's own ranking already says markouts first, then recalibrate ('markout study per fee-window; then recalibrate C down'), so on the sequencing question R is right and V's claim as posed is contradicted by V-side data: DATA-PACK's LVR table puts Fables ETH at 1.55% yield/k against a 3.81% sigma^2/8 break-even, i.e. the keeper does not clear it. What R gets wrong is the prior direction: the measured evidence points to fees being under LVR, not over, so 'down ~30%' is not empirically anchored on this pool and should not be presupposed. issues.reasoning: Mechanically orthogonal: TVL wins routed flow (the 720k-TVL 34.99 bps SPY pool takes the most UR flow on the pair), and fee level prices the arb flow. But they are not sequence-independent. Seeding NVDA at 7 bps against a 22-27 bps break-even, with 26-32% of its flow from identified arb contracts, transfers the seed to arbitrageurs; fee should move before capital does. Second interaction: R's pitch for the SPY/NVDA cross is 'we're already the cheapest quote' at 5 bps versus the unhooked 6.25 pool, and V's ProposedFees raises the cross to 900/650/250, which removes that pitch. The flow evidence says being cheapest is not what wins routed flow, so the conflict is rhetorical rather than economic, but R should not sell the cross on price if V's ladder ships.

issues.reasoning: The evidence supports the law but with the 'comparable-fee' qualifier removed. Depth wins routed flow across a very wide fee range: the 34.99 bps SPY pool with the most TVL on the pair takes 74.8% of its volume from the UniversalRouter and the largest 24h volume; the 5 bps NVDA v3 pool with 70x Fables' depth holds 96-99%. Ultra-low fee wins arb regardless of depth: the 1 bp WETH/USDG v3 pool does $200M/day, and Fables' own overnight SPY volume per hour exceeds its in-session volume, which is ES-driven arb at 3.5 bps. The implication R does not follow through on is symmetric: if cutting fees buys no routed flow, raising them loses none; the flow a raise loses is arb flow, which is the flow costing LPs money. R's law is correct; V's action is what it implies. Caveat: the mechanism by which UR prefers the 35 bps pool is unexplained (a quoter should penalise 35 bps on small trades), so treat it as an empirical regularity, not a settled rule.

Both documents are right that an equity-style overnight discount is too deep. R's flat 5/5/3 gives 1.00/1.00/0.60; V's 1500/1000/300 gives 1.00/0.67/0.20. On variance, R is closer on overnight (0.83 vs R 1.0 vs V 0.67) but far off on the weekend (0.068 vs R 0.60 vs V 0.20); on volume-weighted break-even (be_all.json GLD overnight/open 0.38-0.44) V is closer. Summed error favours V. Neither addresses that the hook's session clock is equity hours: CLOSED starts Friday 16:00 ET while gold trades to 17:00 ET, and Sunday 18:00 ET to Monday 00:00 ET prices at closedFloor while GC is live (SessionLib.classify:91-97). MAX_SESSION_LENGTH of 12h (MarketCalendar.sol:110) means a 23h gold session cannot be expressed; the fix is a closedSpike or a shifted session, which neither proposes.

issues.reasoning: R's claim is false on inspection. SessionLib.utcOffsetFromDate (lines 175-184) computes EDT/EST from the second Sunday of March and first Sunday of November; MarketCalendar.dstMode defaults to AUTO (enum value 0, line 44) and is admin-settable to FIXED_EST/FIXED_EDT as an escape hatch. The only imprecision is day-granular resolution on the switch Sunday itself (utcOffset uses the UTC civil date, SessionLib.sol:167-172), which the code comments correctly note falls on a CLOSED day. RecalibrationNvdaSpy.t.sol pins ET instants in EDT (UTC-4). There is no November drift. V makes no claim on DST so the verdict is that R's caveat #4 should be struck.

issues.reasoning: The V-side claim that the keeper's fee yield clears sigma^2/8 is contradicted by the data: from now.json, ETH fees 24h $1,048 on $282.6k TVL gives APR/k = 3.06% (k 44.3) against sigma^2/8 = 3.78% at 55% vol; on 7d it is 0.77%. DATA-PACK sec 5 reports the same (1.55% vs 3.81%). R's caveats are correct that fees/volume is revenue not LP P&L and that markouts are the real test. However R's own sequencing (R:115, 'markout study per fee-window; then recalibrate') means recalibrating C down is NOT justified now, and the 30% figure is a literature prior (arXiv 2404.05803 could not be verified locally), not a measurement. Lowering C on a pool that already fails to clear sigma^2/8 would widen the gap unless markouts show realised loss is well below the formula. The keeper series (lvr24h.json) has f/s^2 median 0.40 pips per (% annualised)^2, range 0.17-0.75, so the effective C is already not a single constant; any recalibration must first pin what C currently is. R's '450 -> 671 in 27 minutes' is consistent with the series (450 and 671 both present).

issues.reasoning: Mostly orthogonal but not fully. Seeding TVL into NVDA (R:47-49, 114) and raising NVDA's fee interact in two ways: higher fee APR is what attracts and retains seeded TVL (NVDA is currently losing to LVR, be2.py), which is complementary; but seeded depth only captures routed flow if the quote wins, and NVDA at 1000-1400 pips is 2-3x the 500-pip v3 holding 97.5% of the pair, so the raise shrinks the routed flow the seed is meant to catch. On the SPY/NVDA cross, ProposedFees.t.sol:37 proposes 900/650/250 while R's whole case for seeding the cross is that Fables is 'already the cheapest quote' at 5 bps vs the 6.25-bps incumbent (R:37, 89); raising to 9 bps removes that advantage, so there IS a direct conflict on the cross. Both documents fail to mention this.
issues.would_change_my_mind: Evidence that cross-pair flow is arb rather than routed retail, which would make the cheapest-quote advantage irrelevant.

issues.reasoning: The first half of the law (depth wins comparable-fee routed flow) is supported: NVDA v3 at 500 pips with 70x Fables' TVL holds 97.5% (now.json); the same-fee AAPL claim is asserted but not locally verifiable. The second half is weaker: within SPY, the 625-pip pool at $500k holds 70% over 7d while the 3499-pip pool at comparable-to-larger depth holds 20%, so among comparable depths fee DOES move share; and the 3499-pip SPY pool receives 74% of its swaps from the UniversalRouter (ur_now.json), so 'ultra-low fee wins arb flow regardless of depth' is not the whole picture: a 35 bps pool is getting routed flow. The law does NOT imply a raise is free. UR is price-sensitive by construction and now carries 17-51% of Fables swaps, so V's 'we have essentially none to lose' (V:103) is superseded by V's own addendum. R never claims the raise is free; it claims cutting buys nothing, which the evidence supports.
